label: Staying route
title: Your staying route
promise: Build the life you want where you are.
intro_title: Why staying needs a plan too
intro: Staying can be the best result of this Blueprint. But staying and changing nothing is not the same as building the life you want where you are. A change at home needs the same care as a move: a date, an order, money that works, people on board, and a way to check that it helps.

This part turns your decision into a plan. It is shorter than the moving steps, because you keep your home, your papers and your surroundings. What changes is how you use them. Use this part if your decision was "go and change where I am". Moving? Skip it and continue with Step 4.
route_title: Only if you stay: plan your change where you are
can_skip: Only if you are staying. If your decision was to move, skip this part and continue with Step 4.

finish.title: My Change Plan
finish.description: Your change where you are, with a date, a first step and a check-in.

start_here.prompt: Pick the date your change should be in place. Then count back: what has to happen first, and how long does it take? Think of a conversation with your employer, a notice period, a course, your first clients, or saving a buffer.

example.text: Change: four days a week from 1 March, with Fridays for my ceramics studio. Steps: talk to my manager in October; try a ceramics course in November to test the idea; review our budget with my partner in December; submit a formal request for four days in January, with two months' notice; my first Friday in the studio on 3 March.

exercises.title: Money and work

fields.label: My income after the change, and from when
Costs that start or stop
The buffer I keep
The conversation I need to have, and with whom
Questions for an adviser: tax, pension, social security

start_here.prompt: In Part 1 you checked whether the money carries your change. Now make it concrete: what changes in your income, and from when? Which costs start or stop? And which conversation do you need to have first?

tips: Working fewer hours or starting a business can change your tax, your pension and your social security. Ask your employer, your pension fund or an adviser before you sign anything.

fields.label: Hours of "my choice" per week now, and after the change
What I change at home: space, the garden, a room for my work
Must-dos I stop, share or simplify
Two blocks of my week I take back first.

start_here.prompt: Your home and your week are where a change becomes real. In Step 1 you sorted your week into time fixed by others, must-dos and your own choice. Look at it again: what moves to "my choice" after this change?

fields.label: Who I tell, and when
What I need from my partner or family
Who already lives the way I want, and what I will ask them

start_here.prompt: The people around you notice a change at home as much as a move. Tell them what you are changing, why, and what you need from them. Some will cheer you on, and some will not understand. Look for people who already live the way you want to: they are your best source of advice.

fields.label: The first thing I do in week one
What I want to be true after 30 days
What I want to be true after 90 days
What I will say no to, to protect the change

start_here.prompt: The first months decide whether a change sticks. Old habits pull you back, and work fills the free time again. Plan your first 90 days on purpose.

exercises.title: Check in: is it working?

bullets: Do my ordinary days look more like my Life Picture than before?
What is my next change, or is this enough for now?

fields.label: My two check-in dates: three months and one year after the change

start_here.prompt: Put two dates in your calendar: three months and one year after the change. On those dates, read your Life Picture from Step 1 again, and ask yourself three questions:

exercises.closing: If the answer disappoints you, you have not failed. You have learned what does not work, and that is the start of your next plan. And if the change works and you still want more, look at Step 2 again. Maybe your next step is a move after all.

talk: Ask the person closest to you two questions. What do you think will change for you? And what do you need from me?

example_page.lead: A completed page. Rosa from Step 1 is made up. She tested her change in Step 2, and her decision in Part 4 was "Go, and change where I am". This is her Change Plan. Every line is filled in, including what is still uncertain.
rows: The change I am making
Four days a week at my current job, with Fridays outside.
What I keep
My job and my team, our rented flat, my parents twenty minutes away, and Sunday dinners with them.
The date it is in place.
1 March.
The small test I run first
Six Friday afternoons of unpaid leave, from January to mid-February. Errands move to Thursday evening.
My first three steps, and when
Talk to my manager in November. Redo our budget at 80% with my partner in December. Submit the formal request in January, with two months' notice.
Money and time after the change: income, buffer, and hours that become mine

Take-home pay drops by about €420 a month. We cut €300: the second car and fewer meals out. The last €120 comes from our buffer for now, under the €150 we set in Step 1. My choice goes from about 30 to 38 hours a week.
Who I tell, and what I need from them
My partner: help me keep Fridays free. My manager: a clear handover on Thursdays. My parents: lunch on Friday, every other week.
My first 90 days
Week one: a walk on Friday morning, phone off. After 30 days: no work email on Fridays. After 90 days: outside every Friday, and still within budget.
What is still uncertain
Whether my workload shrinks with my hours. Whether the budget holds once the winter energy bills arrive.
My Plan B
If work spills into my Fridays for more than a month, I ask my manager for a review. If nothing changes, I look at other jobs here before anything bigger.
My check-in dates
1 June, and 1 March next year.
